description:
FILED s539b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16) from the port-4 D0 prediction: the binder (InterpScan, form `deref`, canon `$x`) records `$$x[1]` as a use of the SCALAR $x, the fixer's scalar arm `\$x\b(?![\[\{])` skips it.  PRE-EXISTING on main d2bc17d4.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s539b/pr/r1.pl in the s539b worktree; perl 5.40.3):

    my $a = [1, 2]; my $h = { k => 'v' };
    print "$$a[1] @$a[0,1] ${$a}[0] $$h{k}\n";    # perl: 2 1 2 1 v
    sub f { my $s = shift; return "$$s[0]|@$s[1,0]" }
    print f([7, 8]), "\n";                         # perl: 7|8 7
    my $c = [5, 6];
    package Q;
    print "$$c[1] @$c[0,1]\n";                     # perl: 6 5 6

main d2bc17d4: `Transpile failed: PCL internal: the span rename of $c left a use unrenamed at line 7` (a loud refusal of valid perl); without the last three lines: ` 1 2 1 v` -- `my $a` is the exception rename's (`$a__excl__0`) and "$$a[1]" / "@$a[0,1]" kept reading the special `$a`.

FIX (s539b): one arm before the element exclusion -- a `$` or `@` cast followed by `$x` and a subscript is the scalar $x: `(?<!\\)((?:\\\\)*)([\$\@])\$x\b(?=[\[\{])`.  The backslash parity guard is the cast's own (`\$$x[0]` is text `$` + an element of @x).

=== s539b: the SECOND face, braced names (docs/interp-scan.md divergence 2, perl bug #20716) ===
A braced NAME closes the reference in interpolated text -- "${x}[0]" is $x then "[0]", "@{x}{" is @x then "{" (probed perl 5.40.3: `my $a="A"; my @a=("E0"); my %a=(k=>"HK"); print "${a}[0] ${a}{k} ${a}{ @{a}[0]"` prints `A[0] A{k} A{ E0[0]`).  The fixer's `$` arm excluded `${x}[` / `${x}{`, its `@` arm renamed `${x}[` as an element of @x and excluded `@{x}{`, its `%` arm renamed `${x}{` / `@{x}{` as %x.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s539b/pr/b1.pl): perl t/comp/parser.t's #20716 block under the exception rename of `my $a`, and a promoted file `my $x` read braced in a named sub:

    { my $a = "A"; my @b = ("B"); print "${a}{|${a}[|@{b}{|${a}[0]|@{b}[0]\n"; }   # perl A{|A[|B{|A[0]|B[0]   main {|[|B{|[0]|B[0]
    my @x = (1, 2); my $x = 'S';
    sub f { my @x = (7); "${x}[0] $x[0] @{x}[0]" }
    print f(), "\n";                                                                 # perl S[0] 7 7[0]   main [0] 7 7[0]

FIX (s539b): the braced arms take no subscript lookahead and belong to the sigil they spell (`${x}` -> $x, `@{x}` -> @x, `$#{x}` -> @x); the `${x}[` arm of the array family and the braced arm of the hash family are deleted.

=== DONE (s539b) ===
_interp_fixer: a braced NAME closes the reference -- the braced arms take no subscript lookahead and belong to the sigil they spell (`${x}` -> $x, `@{x}` -> @x, `$#{x}` -> @x); the `${x}[` arm of the array family and the braced arm of the hash family are deleted -- and a scalar deref with a subscript is the scalar's (`(?<!\\)((?:\\\\)*)([\$\@])\$x\b(?=[\[\{])`).  docs/interp-scan.md divergence 2 CLOSED.  Population effect: t/comp/parser.t (the #20716 block: the exception-renamed `my $a` read as "${a}{" / "${a}[" in a string, an s/// replacement and a heredoc) -- a silent wrong under the old walk, a rule-12 refusal under the port alone; committed BEFORE the port.  Guards Pl/t/rename-binder-01.t rows 6-9 (fail on c1fe4930).
subject: The rename families' interpolation fixer (Parser2::_interp_fixer) read interpolated text unlike perl: a SCALAR DEREF with a subscript ("$$x[0]", "@$x[1,2]", "$$x{k}") was skipped as an element of @x, and a braced NAME with a subscript ("${x}[0]", "${x}{", "@{x}{" -- perl #20716: the braces close the reference) was taken for an element or a slice -- after an exception / state / shadow / capture rename the text read the OLD variable (silent: empty) and the span pass refused the file -- pre-existing; fixed s539b
